strengths: The path-measure perspective provides a useful conceptual unification of diffusion density estimation and SMC control, with explicit connections to Itô estimators, Feynman–Kac methods, and twisted diffusion sampling.
The analytical reference process is a practical stabilization technique. Comparisons across discretizations and importance-sampling budgets help demonstrate its benefits and limitations.

Experiments cover density estimation, annealing, composition, and reward tilting. The ALDP energy-TVD improvement from 0.338 for FKC to 0.034 for tuned RNC is substantial, and the proposal/target coefficient sweeps provide useful empirical analysis.
weaknesses: The claimed exact correction for imperfect models is generally incorrect for annealing and composition. Appendix A.2 sets q_target(z|x) = p(z|x)^beta, which is not a normalized conditional distribution. Its normalizer Z_beta(x) = integral p(z|x)^beta dz generally depends on x and cannot be discarded from importance weights. Consequently, Eq. (27) targets a marginal proportional to p(x)^beta Z_beta(x), rather than the claimed p(x)^beta. The analogous cancellation underlying Eq. (41) has the same problem. This invalidates a substantive claimed generalization of TDS; the reward-tilting case does not share this particular defect.

The convergence analysis needs correction and more precise assumptions. Appendix A.4 announces an O(delta-t) rate, whereas Proposition A.2 states an O(sqrt(delta-t)) L2 rate. The proposition assumes bounded moments, while the proof additionally invokes Lipschitz coefficients and bounds on inverse diffusion coefficients. It also specializes the trajectory to the model's backward drift despite the broader statement about Y.

Practical density-estimation evidence is limited to a 10-dimensional Gaussian mixture with analytical scores. There is no evaluation of density accuracy for learned, imperfect scores, although the manuscript acknowledges potentially arbitrary errors in this setting. PF-ODE likelihood estimation is not included as an accuracy/cost baseline, and the claimed broader applicability to bridge models and stochastic interpolants is not demonstrated experimentally.

Evidence of improvement over existing control methods is uneven. Table 2's tuned RNC improves some metrics, but FKC remains better on docking-score product and worst-pocket score. The reported variability does not establish the significance of these differences. Reward tilting is compared only against unconditional sampling, omitting directly relevant TDS/Feynman–Kac steering and simple reward-based resampling baselines.

Hyperparameter selection and computational comparisons are insufficiently controlled. The strongest annealing result follows a coefficient sweep without a clearly separated selection protocol or comparably tuned baseline. Wall-clock and network-evaluation measurements are absent despite claims of minimal overhead. Diversity loss remains material: every SMC method in Table 1 has worse sample W2 than the uncorrected baseline, and this should remain part of the assessment of distributional fidelity.

Much of the theoretical contribution reformulates established time-reversal, importance-sampling, and SMC identities. The unification is valuable, but its incremental novelty, the incorrect exactness claim, and incomplete practical validation leave insufficient support for acceptance. Reproducibility also needs clarification: Section 5 describes ALDP training at 800 K, whereas Appendix D.1 describes collecting its dataset at 300 K.

strengths: The path-measure perspective provides a useful conceptual connection between diffusion density estimation, importance sampling, and existing SMC guidance methods. The manuscript explicitly relates its framework to Itô estimators, Feynman–Kac methods, and twisted diffusion sampling.

The analytical reference process addresses a concrete numerical instability. The density-estimation experiments include relevant comparisons across discretizations, reference-process choices, and importance-sampling sample counts.

The experiments show promising practical results, particularly the ALDP energy TV improvement from 0.338 for FKC to 0.034 for the selected RNC configuration. The appendix also examines particle diversity and sensitivity to proposal parameters.
weaknesses: The claimed exact correction for imperfect models has a substantive normalization error. In Appendix A.2, following Eq. (44), the authors choose q_target(z|x) = p(z|x)^β. This is generally not a normalized conditional density: it requires division by Zβ(x) = ∫p(z|x)^β dz, which generally depends on x. Omitting that factor changes the endpoint target from p(x)^β to a distribution proportional to p(x)^β Zβ(x). Consequently, Eq. (27) and Proposition A.1 do not establish exact annealing correction as claimed; analogous problems affect the product/CFG extension. The reward-tilting case with an unpowered conditional does not suffer from this particular issue.

The convergence analysis needs substantial repair. Appendix A.4 announces an O(Δt) rate, whereas Proposition A.2 states O(√Δt) in L2. Its statement assumes bounded moments, but the proof additionally invokes Lipschitz and linear-growth conditions. The proof also specializes the trajectory to drift ν despite the broader formulation, and the log-concavity inequality in Eq. (81) has the wrong direction; the subsequent squared bound does not follow. These issues undermine the stated theoretical guarantee.

The practical density-estimation evidence is narrow: it uses a single 10-dimensional Gaussian mixture with analytical scores. This does not establish robustness to learned-score errors, high dimensionality, or the nonlinear bridge/interpolant settings used to motivate greater flexibility. A probability-flow ODE likelihood baseline and comparisons at matched computational cost are missing.

The gains over the strongest control baseline are not consistently convincing. In Table 2, the selected RNC configuration improves some metrics, but FKC remains better on the docking-score product and worst-pocket docking score. Results use only 32 ligands per target pair, with substantial variability and no paired uncertainty analysis establishing the claimed improvement. Reward tilting is compared only with uncontrolled sampling, despite the close relationship to TDS and Feynman–Kac steering.

Distributional accuracy is insufficiently established. Table 1 reports worse sample W2 for every SMC method than for the uncorrected baseline, while emphasizing histogram metrics that can conceal missing modes. Appendix B.2 itself demonstrates that favorable energy histograms can coexist with severe mode collapse. These observations require stronger joint-distribution and mode-coverage evaluation before claiming faithful target sampling.

Much of the foundation reformulates established time-reversal and importance-sampling identities. The potentially valuable additions are broader process choices and reference-based discretization, but their advantages are not isolated sufficiently through matched tuning budgets, held-out parameter selection, or runtime measurements. Combined with the incorrect exactness claim, the evidence does not support acceptance at a top-tier venue.

strengths: The path-measure perspective provides a useful conceptual unification of diffusion density estimation and SMC control, with explicit connections to Itô estimators, Feynman–Kac methods, and twisted diffusion sampling.
The analytical reference process addresses a concrete numerical instability. The density-estimation ablations examine reference processes, discretization, and importance-sampling sample counts.

The ALDP result is promising: energy TVD decreases from 0.338 for FKC to 0.034 for the selected RNC configuration. Experiments also cover model composition and reward tilting, with useful discussion of particle diversity.
weaknesses: The claimed exact correction for imperfect models has a substantive mathematical flaw. Appendix A.2 sets q_target(z|x) = p(z|x)^β after Eq. (44), but this is generally not a normalized conditional density. Normalization requires Zβ(x) = ∫p(z|x)^β dz, which generally depends on x and cannot be dropped from importance weights. Consequently, Eq. (27)/(39) generally targets a marginal proportional to p(x)^β Zβ(x), rather than p(x)^β. The product/CFG extension has the analogous problem. This invalidates an important claimed guarantee and the interpretation of RNC-TDS for these tasks; the reward-tilting case does not have this particular defect.

The remaining flexible correction relies on exact time reversal, whereas practical pretrained models violate that assumption. The paper acknowledges potentially arbitrary density errors but provides neither quantitative robustness bounds nor controlled experiments varying score error. Thus, the practical reliability of the central density-ratio approximation remains insufficiently established.

Density estimation is evaluated only on a 10-dimensional Gaussian mixture with analytical scores. There is no learned-model likelihood evaluation, higher-dimensional scaling study, or accuracy-versus-compute comparison with probability-flow ODE estimation. The asserted applicability to broader bridge and flow models is not experimentally demonstrated.

Evidence of superiority over established control methods is mixed. In Table 2, the selected RNC configuration improves the better-than-known fraction from 0.608 to 0.649, but FKC remains better on the docking-product and worst-pocket metrics. Only 32 ligands per target pair are generated, and repeated-run or paired uncertainty analysis is absent. Reward tilting is compared only with unconditional sampling, despite the paper's explicit connections to existing reward-steering methods.

The strongest annealing result follows a substantial parameter sweep without a clear held-out selection protocol or comparable baseline tuning budget. Distributional fidelity also remains uncertain: RNC's ALDP W2 is worse than uncorrected sampling, and the appendix shows that favorable energy histograms can coexist with mode collapse. These tradeoffs weaken conclusions drawn primarily from energy TVD.

strengths: The path-measure perspective provides a useful unification of diffusion density estimation, SMC control, and energy regularization. Computing weights through transition-kernel ratios offers a practical, reusable implementation that accommodates different proposal and auxiliary processes without task-specific divergence calculations.

The analytical reference process is a meaningful numerical improvement. Appendices F and G compare estimators across discretizations and sample counts, demonstrating improved density estimates while also documenting situations where the reference introduces additional bias.

Several empirical improvements are substantial: ALDP energy TVD decreases from 0.338 with FKC to 0.034 with tuned RNC; regularization improves learned-energy MCMC sample W2 from 0.9472 to 0.1836; and the free-energy estimate moves considerably closer to the reference value.

The paper distinguishes exact reward-tilting weights for imperfect models from the stronger assumptions needed for annealing and composition. Experiments include synthetic distributions, molecular sampling, ligand design, and a stochastic-interpolant application, supported by extensive derivations and implementation details.
weaknesses: The novelty is primarily a unifying formulation and practical discretization rather than a new underlying identity. The central estimator follows from time reversal and Bayes' rule, and the paper acknowledges that prior work already contains the continuous estimator and a Gaussian-kernel formulation. The incremental contribution beyond these methods needs sharper positioning.

The principal annealing and composition guarantees require exact time reversal, which learned models do not provide. The paper acknowledges this limitation but does not quantify how score error affects weight bias or test robustness across model quality and discretization. Increasing particle count cannot eliminate this error, limiting the interpretation of the inference-time scaling results.

The strongest annealing result depends on selecting proposal coefficients through a substantial sweep, without a clearly specified held-out selection protocol or accounting for tuning cost. Distributional fidelity also remains uncertain: the uncorrected baseline has better sample W2 in Table 1, and Appendix F explicitly demonstrates that favorable energy histograms can coexist with mode collapse. Diversity loss is a substantive sampling limitation.

The ligand-design evidence for improvement over FKC is mixed. The better-than-known fraction increases from 0.608 to 0.649, but docking-score product and maximum-pocket-score metrics worsen. With only 32 ligands per target pair, substantial across-pair variability, and no paired uncertainty analysis or repeated-generation assessment, the claimed advantage is not convincingly established.

Some theoretical claims exceed what the supplied proofs establish. Proposition G.1 states limited assumptions but its proof additionally invokes Lipschitz and growth conditions and specializes the trajectory to drift ν. Equations (90)–(91) also use an invalid concavity-to-squared-error bound. Appendix H.5 connects continuous residual identities but does not establish equivalence of the implemented squared, stop-gradient regularizer and Fokker–Planck regularization objectives.

Evaluation of the training contribution and computational claims is incomplete. There is no direct experimental comparison with Fokker–Planck regularization, dual score matching is evaluated only on the synthetic energy task, and negligible overhead is asserted without runtime or memory measurements. Sensitivity to regularization strength and time increment, repeated-run uncertainty for most main results, and fuller training/MCMC specifications would strengthen reproducibility.

strengths: The path-measure perspective provides a useful unification of diffusion density estimation, SMC correction, and energy regularisation. Allowing flexible proposal and auxiliary drifts without re-deriving task-specific weights is practically appealing.

Several empirical improvements are substantial: ALDP energy TVD decreases from 0.338 with FKC to 0.034 with tuned RNC, and energy-based MCMC sample W2 improves from 0.9472 to 0.1836 with regularisation. The free-energy experiment provides another meaningful application.
The analytical reference process addresses a concrete numerical instability. Appendices F and G compare alternative discretisations and investigate when the reference helps or hurts.
The manuscript acknowledges imperfect-model bias and particle degeneracy, provides extensive connections to prior work, and includes useful implementation and experimental details.
weaknesses: The convergence guarantee is not established convincingly as written. Proposition G.1 states only bounded-moment assumptions, while its proof invokes additional Lipschitz and growth conditions and silently specialises the trajectory to drift nu. Equation (81) applies Ito isometry inconsistently, and the concavity inequality in Equation (90) has the wrong direction; the squared bound in Equation (91) does not follow. These are substantive gaps in the stated guarantee, beyond presentation issues.

The claimed equivalence between the training regulariser and Fokker–Planck regularisation is insufficiently demonstrated. Appendix H.5 manipulates the continuous-time identity, but does not establish convergence of the actual finite-step squared objective or account for its stop-gradient operation. Equivalence of identities does not imply equivalence of training objectives or optimisation gradients.

The main annealing and composition applications require exact time reversal, which learned models do not provide. The paper acknowledges this limitation but offers neither a quantitative error analysis nor controlled experiments varying score error. Increasing particle count cannot eliminate this bias. The exact imperfect-model construction applies only to reward tilting and recovers existing methods.

The incremental contribution over prior work needs stronger validation. The underlying density-ratio identity is standard, and several derived estimators explicitly recover previous results. Consequently, the practical flexibility, numerical stabilisation, and inexpensive regularisation carry much of the novelty. Yet there is no direct experimental comparison against the closely related Fokker–Planck regulariser, and dual score matching is compared only on the synthetic 100D example.

The inference-time comparisons do not fully establish robust superiority. RNC benefits from a substantial coefficient sweep, without a clearly separated validation procedure or comparably documented tuning budget for FKC. In Table 3, the improved better-than-known fraction is accompanied by worse mean docking-product and worst-pocket metrics than FKC; paired uncertainty analysis is needed to support the claimed gain. Appendix F.3 also demonstrates that favourable energy histograms can coexist with severe mode collapse, weakening reliance on that metric.

Efficiency and reproducibility evidence remain incomplete. Claims of negligible overhead are unsupported by measured training time, sampling time, memory, or matched-compute comparisons. Important details such as optimisation schedules for the energy experiments and MCMC settings are missing, and several headline results lack variability across independent runs. The CTMC extension has no empirical validation.

strengths: The path-measure perspective provides a useful unification of diffusion density estimation, SMC correction, and energy regularization. The connections to existing estimators and correctors are explained extensively.

The analytical reference process is a practical contribution supported by density-estimation ablations. Allowing flexible proposal and auxiliary drifts also expands the design space beyond the particular FKC construction.

Several results are substantial: ALDP energy TVD improves from 0.338 with FKC to 0.034 with tuned RNC, and regularization improves MCMC sample W2 from 0.9472 to 0.1836 while preserving diffusion sampling quality. The free-energy experiment provides additional evidence of improved energy learning.
The manuscript explicitly acknowledges imperfect-score bias and particle degeneracy, and provides extensive derivations and supplementary experiments.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is narrower than the framing suggests. The central identity follows from standard time reversal, and several resulting algorithms recover existing methods. Acceptance therefore depends heavily on demonstrating the value of the flexible discretization and regularizer; the current comparisons do not sufficiently establish that value.

The convergence guarantee is not established as stated. Proposition G.1 assumes bounded moments, but its proof additionally invokes Lipschitz and growth conditions and specializes the trajectory to drift ν rather than an arbitrary proposal. Equation (90) reverses the concavity inequality, and Equation (91) does not follow by squaring a one-sided bound. The introductory O(Δt) claim also needs to be distinguished from the O(√Δt) L2 bound in Equation (69).

The energy-training evaluation omits the closest baseline, Fokker–Planck regularization, despite claiming an equivalent and cheaper alternative. Dual score matching is evaluated only on the 100D GMM. There are no measured runtime or memory comparisons supporting negligible overhead, nor sensitivity studies for regularization strength and time increment. Appendix H.5 connects continuous identities without establishing equivalence of the implemented finite-step, stop-gradient training objectives.

The strongest inference-time improvement uses coefficients selected through a sweep on the evaluated ALDP target, without a clear held-out selection protocol or accounting for tuning cost. Table 1 lacks uncertainty estimates. Table 3 shows mixed results against FKC: RNC improves the fraction better than reference ligands but worsens the docking-product and worst-pocket metrics, with substantial reported variability and no paired uncertainty analysis.

Correctness for annealing and composition requires exact scores; increasing particle count does not remove learned-model bias. Although acknowledged, this limitation is not quantified experimentally. Furthermore, favorable energy histograms do not establish recovery of the full target distribution: Appendix F.3 itself illustrates good energy agreement despite mode collapse.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the lengthy appendix. Important energy-model training settings and MCMC sampling details are missing, and the main text describes ALDP annealing from an 800K-trained model while Appendix I.1 describes a 300K dataset without explaining the discrepancy. Overall, the promising results do not yet compensate for the unresolved theoretical and comparative-evaluation gaps.
